thread:
nina: URGENT: we detected anomalous code-signing activity for org key CS-ORG-01. Immediate actions required for all teams that publish signed artifacts.

nina: What we saw: CI job `release/sign` used the org signing key at an unexpected time and from an unfamiliar runner IP. We're treating this as suspected credential exposure.

sam: Do we think the private key was leaked or is it a compromised runner?
nina: Investigation in progress. For now assume compromise until proven otherwise. We are revoking the current key and issuing a replacement.

jess: Action items for app/platform teams?
nina: 1) Stop trusting current signatures from CS-ORG-01 effective immediately. 2) Rebuild any artifacts signed in the last 48h and re-sign with the new key once published. 3) Verify CI runners and runners' machine images; rotate runner tokens. 4) If you have pinned signatures in deployment manifests, update verification policy to accept the new key fingerprint.

infra-oncall-bot: Automated response: revoking key CS-ORG-01 now and creating temp signing key CS-TEMP-XXXX. Expect rotation bulletin in 30 minutes.

jess: How do we verify which artifacts used the old key?
nina: Use our artifact index and signature metadata: search for `signing_key_id: CS-ORG-01` in the artifact store. Example query: `curl -s https://internal.redwood/artifacts/search?signing_key=CS-ORG-01`

sam: Will there be a grace window for deploys that validate signatures?
nina: We are publishing a short grace policy: deployment verifiers should reject CS-ORG-01 after revocation. If you absolutely must allow a specific deploy, open an eng-security ticket with justification; exceptions are time-limited.

ops-bot: Canaries: revocation propagated to verification service @ 14:12 UTC :white_check_mark:

jess: CI changes needed? Our pipeline calls `sign-tool` with a service account key.
nina: Replace uses of the long-lived signing key with the ephemeral signing flow: 1) CI requests a short-lived signing token from Signing Service (OIDC -> sign API), 2) sign-tool uses token to sign, 3) token TTL 15m. We will post docs and example steps in the next 20m.

infra-oncall-bot: Scan result: 9 artifacts signed with CS-ORG-01 in last 48h. Tickets created: https://internal.redwood/engsec/tickets/RED-6009

sam: Any advice for verifying deployed containers that might have been signed by the old key?
nina: Run verification locally: `cosign verify --key <new-key-pub> <image>` and check metadata for `signing_key_id`. For images signed with CS-ORG-01, rebuild and re-sign. If rebuilding isn't possible immediately, isolate the service and escalate.

jess: ETA for new key publication?
nina: New org key published to KMS-backed store and verification service updated at 14:40 UTC. We'll publish fingerprints and rotation steps.

infra-oncall-bot: Reminder: if you detect suspicious runner activity, revoke runner token and file a ticket with `code-signing-incident` prefix.

nina: Thank you all. We'll follow up with a postmortem and IOCs once the investigation completes. Closing this thread for signal; keep tickets updated.
